title: vSAN Cluster Health Test Findings
exclusions: Covers the cached overall result returned by `Test-VsanClusterHealth`; it does not enumerate every failing test, prove data loss or application outage, monitor non-vSAN datastores, authorize repair, or equate gray/unknown with healthy. Cached result age and collection health matter. The legacy unsupported `vmware:perf:vsan` `health_status`/`disk_group` contract is not used.
evidence: Retain PowerCLI script/module version and hash, credential/role design, scripted-input schedule/heartbeat, raw JSON and latest successful poll, matching vSphere Skyline Health/PowerCLI detail, versioned search and rows, incident disposition, and dated green/yellow/red/unknown, stale cache, null field, duplicate, unavailable service and recovery tests. Documentation review generated no vSAN fault or runtime proof.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Index a fresh complete fixture for cluster `domain-c8` with overall_status `yellow`, description `One or more health checks require attention`, score 80 and valid test time. Expect exactly one high-severity `non_green_vsan_health` row retaining description and score.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero primary rows for green status, collection older than 20 minutes, blank cluster identity/status, invalid test time, wrong source/index, or exact replay. Unknown/gray-like statuses must remain visible when fresh and must never be converted to green.

dataSources: Local VMware PowerCLI scripted input with Splunk Add-on for VMware (Splunkbase 3215) inventory/events as context. `index=vmware-ops`, `sourcetype=vmware:powercli:vsan_health`; required fields: cluster_id, cluster_name, overall_status, overall_description, health_score, time_of_test, vcenter. The fields map to documented VsanClusterHealthTestResult properties OverallHealthStatus, OverallHealthDescription, HealthScore, TimeOfTest.
app: Splunk Add-on for VMware (`Splunk_TA_vmware` and `SA-Hydra`, Splunkbase 3215) for vCenter API collection; Splunk Add-on for VMware Indexes (Splunkbase 5640) and Splunk Add-on for VMware Extractions (Splunkbase 5641) are deployment components required by current packaging. A local virtualization-operations app owns searches, lookups, dashboards, scripted inputs where stated, and runbooks.
spl:
index=vmware-ops sourcetype="vmware:powercli:vsan_health" earliest=-30m
| eval cluster_id=trim(cluster_id), cluster_name=trim(cluster_name), overall_status=lower(trim(overall_status)), health_score=tonumber(health_score), test_epoch=strptime(time_of_test,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%Q%z")
| where len(cluster_id)>0 AND len(cluster_name)>0 AND len(overall_status)>0 AND isnotnull(test_epoch)
| stats latest(overall_status) as overall_status latest(overall_description) as overall_description latest(health_score) as health_score latest(test_epoch) as test_epoch latest(_time) as collection_time latest(vcenter) as vcenter by cluster_id cluster_name
| eval collection_age_minutes=round((now()-collection_time)/60,1)
| where overall_status!="green" AND collection_age_minutes<=20
| eval use_case_id="UC-2.1.10", finding="non_green_vsan_health", local_severity=case(overall_status="red","critical",overall_status="yellow","high",true(),"medium")
| convert ctime(test_epoch)
| table cluster_name cluster_id vcenter overall_status overall_description health_score test_epoch collection_age_minutes finding local_severity use_case_id
| sort 0 cluster_name
description: Reports a vSAN cluster when a fresh PowerCLI `Test-VsanClusterHealth -UseCache` result has an overall status other than green, preserving the documented overall description, score, test time, and stable cluster identity.
value: A non-green vSAN health summary can reveal degraded protection, disk, network, configuration, capacity, or health-service conditions that threaten storage resilience. A faithful summary routes teams to the exact test detail without inventing a disk-group status field.
implementation: Deploy a local PowerCLI scripted input using the documented `Test-VsanClusterHealth` command with `-UseCache`; emit documented result properties to `vmware:powercli:vsan_health` every 10 minutes. Alert on fresh non-green overall status and route to vSAN operations. Drill into individual result components in vCenter/PowerCLI before remediation; use capacity, resync, disk, network and object health as separate supporting contracts.
visualization: Dashboard `vSAN Health`: script heartbeat and cluster coverage first; current status tiles by cluster; table with status, description, score, test/collection age, vCenter, owner, maintenance and incident; drilldowns to individual NetworkHealth, DiskHealthResult, HclInfo, LimitHealth and resync/capacity panels. Default current state with 30-day status-transition history; link to vSphere Cluster > Monitor > vSAN > Skyline Health.

references.title: Broadcom guidance for a full vSAN datastore

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Approved rolling maintenance or patching** — vSAN health can be genuinely non-green while a host or disk group is under maintenance. Confirm exact cluster, maintenance mode choice, task, data evacuation policy, resync state and end time; use a finite cluster exception in `vmware_uc_dispositions.csv` only for notification.

2. **Health-check retest or cache lag** — the cached result may remain non-green briefly after correction. Compare TimeOfTest, run an owner-approved current test, inspect individual results and wait for proven green convergence; never overwrite stale status.

3. **Documented unsupported hardware or HCL warning** — a genuine HCL finding may be accepted temporarily under a hardware plan. Verify the exact test, hardware/driver/firmware evidence, risk owner and expiry; keep the base finding.

4. **Transient network or disk resync condition** — a short component event can produce a real summary warning. Check vSAN resyncing objects, network and disk health plus persistence; resolve the condition or document a bounded operational disposition rather than suppressing all non-green status.

Delivery suppression uses the governed lookup table `vmware_uc_dispositions.csv` only after the base result is retained; each entry requires the exact UC/entity keys, owner, ticket, reason, start, and finite expiry.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and source contract

This is a documentation-reviewed implementation, not a record that the search ran in production. Use Splunk Add-on for VMware (Splunkbase 3215) with its compatible `Splunk_TA_vmware` and `SA-Hydra` packages. Current packaging also requires the VMware Indexes and Extractions packages on the tiers named by Splunk's installation guide. The scheduler assigns API jobs to Data Collection Nodes; a DCN must reach vCenter over HTTPS and forward collected data to the indexer. Use a dedicated vCenter account whose effective privileges have been tested against the inventory, performance, task, or event objects required here. Do not copy an unverified role name from this page.

The indexes in the SPL are Splunk's documented defaults from `ta_vmware_collection.conf`: `index=vmware-perf`, `index=vmware-inv`, and `index=vmware-taskevent`. If local index names differ, change only the base index after proving equivalent routing and access. The relevant documented default tasks are `hostvmperf`, `otherperf`, `datastoreinv`, `vminv`, and `event`; enable only the task named below. Keep vCenter, scheduler, DCNs, indexers, and search heads time-synchronized. Install matching search-time extractions before relying on extracted fields.

## Step 1 — Configure and verify collection

Install a supported VMware PowerCLI module on a controlled Heavy Forwarder and create a local scripted input at 600 seconds. For each governed vSAN-enabled cluster, call `Test-VsanClusterHealth -Cluster <cluster> -UseCache`. Serialize the documented result properties and explicit cluster/vCenter IDs as one JSON event. Emit a separate successful-run heartbeat, because no finding can mean green clusters or failed collection. Do not use the nonexistent `Get-VsanClusterHealth` command.

Before saving the analytic, run a discovery search over at least two expected collection intervals:

```spl
index=vmware-ops (sourcetype="vmware:powercli:vsan_health" OR sourcetype="vmware:powercli:vsan_health:heartbeat") earliest=-30m
| stats count latest(_time) as latest_poll dc(cluster_id) as cluster_count values(overall_status) as statuses by sourcetype
| convert ctime(latest_poll)
```

Confirm the expected entities appear, compare them with the named vSphere or PowerCLI view, and inspect representative `_raw` events. Verify every required field rather than treating a sourcetype count as proof of semantic completeness. Record the add-on version, collection task, configured interval, target index, vCenter, entity scope, and p95/p99 indexing delay. A missing entity or stale poll is a source-health finding and must not be interpreted as a healthy virtualization condition.

## Step 2 — Create and understand the search

Save the sidecar SPL verbatim as `vmware_vsan_non_green_health` after substituting only an approved local index name. Poll every 10 minutes and run the saved search every 10 minutes with enough offset for script completion. Reject observations older than 20 minutes and alert source health independently.

```spl
index=vmware-ops sourcetype="vmware:powercli:vsan_health" earliest=-30m
| eval cluster_id=trim(cluster_id), cluster_name=trim(cluster_name), overall_status=lower(trim(overall_status)), health_score=tonumber(health_score), test_epoch=strptime(time_of_test,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%Q%z")
| where len(cluster_id)>0 AND len(cluster_name)>0 AND len(overall_status)>0 AND isnotnull(test_epoch)
| stats latest(overall_status) as overall_status latest(overall_description) as overall_description latest(health_score) as health_score latest(test_epoch) as test_epoch latest(_time) as collection_time latest(vcenter) as vcenter by cluster_id cluster_name
| eval collection_age_minutes=round((now()-collection_time)/60,1)
| where overall_status!="green" AND collection_age_minutes<=20
| eval use_case_id="UC-2.1.10", finding="non_green_vsan_health", local_severity=case(overall_status="red","critical",overall_status="yellow","high",true(),"medium")
| convert ctime(test_epoch)
| table cluster_name cluster_id vcenter overall_status overall_description health_score test_epoch collection_age_minutes finding local_severity use_case_id
| sort 0 cluster_name
```

Understanding this SPL: The search validates explicit contract fields and ISO test time, retains the latest result per cluster, rejects stale collection, and returns every fresh status other than exact green. Severity is a local routing map; description and detailed component objects remain authoritative for diagnosis.

The query emits stable columns and preserves the observed values needed for triage. Its threshold or status filter is an explicit local monitoring policy, not a VMware universal limit unless the cited VMware source says otherwise. Keep the unsuppressed result as evidence. Apply delivery suppression only after the row exists through a governed `vmware_uc_dispositions.csv` lookup keyed by `use_case_id` plus the exact entity key, with owner, ticket, reason, start time, and finite `exception_until`; expired, malformed, or wildcard entries must not suppress.

## Step 3 — Validate semantics and controls

Compare every governed cluster with PowerCLI `Test-VsanClusterHealth -UseCache` and vSphere Client **Cluster > Monitor > vSAN > Skyline Health**. Confirm status, score, description and TimeOfTest. Use synthetic JSON for red/yellow/green boundaries; do not create a production vSAN fault solely to test monitoring. Validate a stale-cache/source-failure case separately.

Run the positive and negative `controlTest` scenarios in an isolated search index or lab vCenter. Assert the exact row count and output fields. Also test duplicate input, null required fields, wrong sourcetype/index, events outside the scheduled window, late indexing, and reruns. Compare raw values with the authoritative vSphere Client or PowerCLI result identified above. Measure source coverage, latest event age, duplicate rate, field-null rate, scheduler skips, search runtime, and alert delivery. Keep `status=draft` until VMware, Splunk, service ownership, and operations reviewers approve the data contract and runtime results.

## Step 4 — Operationalize and investigate

Validate heartbeat and test age; open the exact non-green health result; identify affected component/test and scope; check resyncing objects, capacity/slack space, disk groups/devices, network partitions, HCL/driver/firmware and cluster configuration; protect workload and data according to VMware/vSAN runbooks; coordinate repair; rerun health; close only after current green or an explicit risk-owned finite disposition.

Use the dashboard design in `visualization`. Put source health before findings so silence cannot render as green. Restrict raw event, user, VM, datastore, and infrastructure identifiers to roles with an operational need. Alert titles must describe the observed metric, state, or event; they must not claim root cause, outage, data loss, unauthorized activity, or successful remediation without corroboration.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot safely

If the script calls `Get-VsanClusterHealth`, correct it to documented `Test-VsanClusterHealth`. If module/cmdlet is unavailable, verify PowerCLI installation/version and vCenter connection. If health is null, inspect permissions and result serialization. If cached data is old, distinguish health-service/cache problems from Splunk delay. If vCenter shows detail but Splunk only summary, add separately reviewed component serialization rather than inventing disk_group fields.

For no data, verify the exact collection task in the scheduler, DCN assignment and health, vCenter credential reach, API scope, target index, extraction package, and time synchronization. Splunk documents that inventory JSON can exceed the default `spath` extraction cutoff; inspect `_raw` and adjust the supported search-command limit only when truncation is demonstrated. For stale or partial inventory, remember that the add-on performs full inventory followed by change sets and later full refreshes. For missing VM performance, verify hierarchy collection and the generated VM managed-object list. Do not change vSphere resources merely to make a monitor pass.

Closure requires a healthy source contract, a reconciled authoritative view, a documented owner decision, and an observed recovery or accepted finite exception. This UC performs no automatic vMotion, restart, snapshot removal, datastore expansion, alarm reset, host remediation, or vSAN repair.
grandmaExplanation: We show when the storage system shared by a cluster says one or more of its health checks needs attention, then direct the team to the detailed check.
